verses.text: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his followers.
He said, "The teachers of the law and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat. They have the job of explaining Moses' Law.
So be careful to do everything they tell you. But do not do what they do, because they do not practise what they teach.
They tie up heavy loads that are hard to carry and put them on other people's shoulders. But they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to help carry them.
"Everything they do is done for people to see. They make the little boxes of Scripture they wear on their foreheads and arms extra wide, and they make the tassels on their clothes extra long.
They love to have the place of honour at dinners and the most important seats in the synagogues.
They love to be greeted with respect in the market places, and to have people call them 'Rabbi'.
"But you should not be called 'Rabbi'. You have only one Teacher, the Christ, and you are all brothers and sisters.
And do not call anyone on earth 'father', because you have one Father, and he is in heaven.
And you should not be called 'master', because you have one Master, the Christ.
The greatest among you will be your servant.
Whoever lifts themselves up will be made humble, and whoever makes themselves humble will be lifted up.

"How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You take away widows' houses, and then you say long prayers to make yourselves look good. So you will be punished even more.

"How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the door of the kingdom of heaven in people's faces. You yourselves do not go in, and you will not let those who are trying to go in enter.

"How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You travel over land and sea to win a single follower. And when you have won them, you make them twice as fit for hell as you are.
"How terrible it will be for you, blind guides! You say, 'If anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing. But anyone who swears by the gold of the temple must keep their promise.'
You blind fools! Which is more important, the gold, or the temple that makes the gold holy?
You also say, 'If anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing. But anyone who swears by the gift on the altar must keep their promise.'
You blind people! Which is more important, the gift, or the altar that makes the gift holy?
So anyone who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.
And anyone who swears by the temple swears by it and by God, who lives in it.
And anyone who swears by heaven swears by God's throne and by God, who sits on it.

"How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You give God a tenth of your spices, like mint, dill and cumin. But you have ignored the more important things in the Law, which are justice, mercy and faithfulness. You should have done these things, without ignoring the others.
You blind guides! You strain a tiny fly out of your drink, but you swallow a whole camel!
"How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of a cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and selfishness.
Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and dish, and then the outside will also be clean.

"How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like tombs that have been painted white. They look beautiful on the outside, but inside they are full of dead people's bones and everything that is unclean.
In the same way, on the outside you seem to be good people. But on the inside you are full of pretending and evil.
"How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets, and you decorate the graves of good people.
And you say, 'If we had lived in the days of our ancestors, we would not have helped them kill the prophets.'
So you are admitting that you are the children of the people who murdered the prophets.
Go on, then, and finish what your ancestors started!
"You snakes! You family of snakes! How will you escape being sentenced to hell?
So I am sending you prophets, wise men and teachers. You will kill some of them and nail some to crosses. You will whip others in your synagogues and chase them from town to town.

And so you will be guilty of the blood of all the good people that has been spilled on earth. This goes from the blood of good Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berekiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.
I tell you for certain, all this will come on the people of today.

"Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You kill the prophets and throw stones at those God sends to you. Many times I have wanted to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings. But you were not willing!
Look, your house is left empty.
I tell you, you will not see me again until you say, 'Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.'"
